subject: Hosted->Dedicated rightsize rehearsal & staged rollout tactics
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@deltahealth.com>, Samir Rao <samir@deltahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted->Dedicated rightsize rehearsal & staged rollout tactics

Hi Alicia / Samir —

Thanks again for the productive call today. Per our discussion, I pulled together a short plan for the "validation + staged rollout" approach that'll let you move from Hosted API to a Dedicated pool with minimal customer impact. High-level asks from you: a steady-state qps profile, a small prompt corpus for quality checks, and procurement timing for a 9-month reserved commit.

Attached: delta_rightsize_workbook_v1.xlsx (proposed telemetry & load profiles), staged_rollout_runbook_v3.md (runbook + playbook).

Proposal summary (two-phase):
- Phase A (Validation, 2 weeks): acceptance load tests at 25/50/75/100% of expected qps, KV cache priming rehearsal, and model variant fallbacks validated.
- Phase B (Staged Rollout, 4-week ramp): canaries (5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%), automated fallback to smaller-quantized variant on perf regressions, and final switch with DNS/traffic cutover window.

Key points we need to align on:
- Exact SLA window for the final cut (we recommend a 3-hour daytime window with rollback triggers).
- Warm-cache strategy: we suggest a 48-hour priming window prior to canary -> production cut.
- Acceptable latency tails for your product (p95/p99 targets).

Next steps:
1) You share qps heatmap + 3 sample prompt sets by EOD Friday.
2) We'll schedule a 90-minute tabletop run-through with your infra team next Wednesday (we'll invite the SREs).
3) Procurement team to confirm milestone billing cadence so we can align provisioning.

Thanks — I want to make the migration predictable and low-friction. If you prefer, we can run a dry-run using a smaller subset of traffic this month to exercise the runbook.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
(Attachment: delta_rightsize_workbook_v1.xlsx, staged_rollout_runbook_v3.md)

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@deltahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@deltahealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@deltahealth.com>
Date: 2028-04-06T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted->Dedicated rightsize rehearsal & staged rollout tactics

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear plan. A few clarifying questions before we finalize dates:
1) Does the 48-hour priming mean we need to hold a mirror of production traffic to the Dedicated pool for two full days? We have concerns about duplicate billing for those requests.
2) For the canary windows, can we shorten the 5% step if the metrics look very clean? Our primary concern is minimizing latency regressions for our clinical workflows.
3) Procurement asked whether the reserved commit can be structured as quarterly usage buckets vs. a single annual prepay.

I can pull the qps heatmap and a 150-prompt validation set by Friday. For the SREs, I can confirm availability for Wed 4/11.

—Alicia
Alicia Gomez
CTO, DeltaHealth
alicia@deltahealth.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@deltahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-07T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted->Dedicated rightsize rehearsal & staged rollout tactics

Alicia — quick answers from the sizing/ops side and a proposed safe default: 

1) Priming: you do not need to mirror full production traffic. Recommended approach: a staged priming script that replays a representative 10-20% sample of historical requests (prefer shorter synthetic bursts to exercise KV sets) over a 48-hour window. We will not charge Hosted API token rates for replayed priming traffic when it's run inside the dry-run unless you request mirrored live traffic; we'll mark those as "test credits" in our billing ledger — we can formalize with Procurement.

2) Canary cadence: you can compress the early steps (5% -> 25% -> 50%) to a single 6-hour observation window if latency/p99 remain within thresholds and error rates < 0.1%. We'll keep automatic rollback triggers in the runtime.

3) Reserved commit: we can offer a quarterly-committed SKU that resets utilization buckets quarterly; discount profile will be slightly lower than an annual prepay but keeps your spend flexibility. Ben will share a pricing sketch.

Sizing excerpt (high level):
- Expected steady-state qps (peak): 450 qps (14B model, avg prompt length 160 tokens).
- Baseline GPU profile suggested: 12 x A100-80GB (in Dedicated pool), balanced across two AZs for failover. That gives us headroom for 1.8x peak with room for autoscale bursts.
- KV cache priming target: 30M tokens across the active prefix sets; expect ~65% cache hit after 48 hours if we replay representative traces.

Attachments: sizing_table_v2.csv (breakdown by horizon + model variant cost).

I'll be on the Wed tabletop to walk through the runbook.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia@deltahealth.com>
Date: 2028-04-09T11:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted->Dedicated rightsize rehearsal & staged rollout tactics

Looping in two quick ops tweaks from my side:
- Runbook change: for the priming step, add a throttling ramp (0.5x -> 1x representative qps) on day 1 to reduce queue buildup on the Dedicated ingress. I've updated staged_rollout_runbook_v3.md with the excerpt (see section 2.1).
- Canary observability: we'll add a transient sampling rule to export full traces for 1 hour at the 25% step so DeltaHealth can validate downstream latency inside their trace sampling. This is a short window and won't change long-term data retention.

Proposed rehearsal dates: dry-run week of Apr 23 (internal prereq work during week of Apr 16). If that works for you, I'll lock infra reservations and a rehearsal runway.

Connor O'Brien
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: staged_rollout_runbook_v3.md [updated])

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Hosted->Dedicated rightsize rehearsal & staged rollout tactics

All —

Thanks for the quick turn. Summary and agreed next steps:
1) DeltaHealth to share qps heatmap + 150 prompt validation set by Fri 4/13.
2) Redwood to provide priming script + non-bill test-credit confirmation for priming replays (action: Karthik).
3) Dry-run scheduling: internal prep week Apr 16; rehearsal (dry-run) Apr 23-27; staged rollout ramp starting May 6 if rehearsal passes.
4) Procurement / Commercial: Ben to send the quarterly-commit pricing sketch and DocuSign for the initial reserved allocation. Procurement team — please confirm milestone billing cadence by 4/17 so we can provision capacity.

Links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/9876543, Runbook (updated): https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-delta-rightsize. DocuSign: https://docusign.com/s/RDW-DELTA-2028 (attached pdf preview docu_sign_proposal_RDW-DELTA-2028.pdf).

If everyone is aligned, Ben and I will run the procurement cadence and Connor/Karthik will lock infra reservations. Appreciate the fast turnaround — we'll keep the rehearsal risk low and automate rollback so customer impact is minimal.

Best,
Marissa
